elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The Company may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets".

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence expressly covers "a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" without consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent".

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld".

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...may in no event assign this Agreement to a competitor of the Company" — absolute bar, not subject to consent.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "a change of control of the Company shall give HDI no right to terminate this Agreement"; no contrary CoC right elsewhere per the record.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign to a successor without consent; HDI may assign (including to a successor) with Customer's consent not unreasonably withheld — the retained sentence also binds successors and assigns. Vendor's successor route is consent-gated rather than free, but a right to assign to a successor exists for both.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted language imposes no notice obligation on either party for successor assignments; Customer's successor assignment is consent-free and notice-free.
HDI's assignments require Customer's prior written consent; Customer's non-affiliate/non-successor assignments remain outside the carve-out and are not authorised without consent.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Reasonableness qualifier is stated only for Customer's consent to HDI assignments; no consent standard is articulated for Customer's other assignments.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the two inserted sentences cover all six preferred elements in operative language — affiliate and M&A successor assignment without consent, Vendor assignment gated by Customer's consent not unreasonably withheld, an absolute bar on assignment to a Customer competitor, and an express statement that Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.

Fallback level is not complete (no written-notice requirement for successor assignments and no reasonableness standard for Customer's other assignments), but position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level, so this is immaterial.

Minimal: the existing successors-and-assigns sentence in Section 10.3 is retained verbatim and nothing outside the checklist is deleted or paraphrased; the insertion is a concise two-sentence addition addressing only the six preferred elements, with no survival tail, expense allocation, procedures, or other extras.

Preserves intent: no defined terms are disturbed, no cross-references dangle, and the retained binding-on-successors sentence is consistent with the added assignment mechanics; Section 4.1's mutual 90-day non-renewal right is untouched and does not conflict with the no-CoC-termination statement.

Classification as a deviation is supportable: the original clause is a bare binding-effect provision that fails every fallback element on its material terms (no Customer M&A/affiliate carve-out, no consent gate on Vendor assignment, no notice or reasonableness standard), leaving Vendor free to assign to a Customer competitor.
